RAINBOW CHILDREN'S MEDICARE Q2 FY27: REVENUE UP 23% YOY; TARGETS 5,000+ BEDS BY FY32, MAJOR HOSPITAL EXPANSION PLANNED

• Hospital Expansion Target: Management plans to expand total bed capacity from 2,685 to 3,875 by FY30, with a target of over 5,000 beds by FY32, including projects under discussion

• Capacity Addition Plans: Targets 25 additional beds in FY27, 385 beds in FY28, 630 beds in FY29 and 150 beds in FY30

• Margin Performance: EBITDA margin stood at 31% versus 33.5% YoY and 28.6% QoQ, reflecting sequential improvement but annual margin pressure

• Hospital Network: Operates 26 hospitals across 11 cities, with total capacity of 2,685 beds, including 130 beds at Madhukar Hospital

• New Hospital Commissioning: Nellore (70 beds) and Guntur (50 beds) commenced operations in September 2026, while Bengaluru HRBR (60 beds) started operations in May 2026

• FY28 Hospital Expansion: Coimbatore hospital targeted for commissioning in H2 FY28, while Mumbai hospital is expected to commence operations in Q1 FY28

• Indore Expansion: Plans to operate 25 beds initially, with an independent approximately 100-bed facility targeted by the end of FY29

• Future Expansion Pipeline: Additional projects under discussion across Hyderabad, Lucknow, Noida, Jaipur, Bhubaneswar, Raipur, Chandigarh, Mumbai and Ludhiana

• Patient Volume Growth: Inpatient discharges increased 15% YoY to 32,706, while outpatient consultations surged 19% to 5.07 lakh

• Maternity Business: Deliveries increased 20% YoY to 5,719, supported by growing demand for women and maternity healthcare services

• Hospital Occupancy: Overall occupancy stood at 49.2% versus 52% YoY and 41.2% QoQ, reflecting strong sequential improvement

• Revenue Per Bed: ARPOB increased 10% YoY to ₹63,413, although it declined from ₹67,256 QoQ

QUALITY POWER Q2 FY27: ₹2,010 CR ORDER BOOK; EBITDA UP 70% YOY, PAT UP 80%, NEW SANGli & TÜRKİYE FACTORIES COMMISSIONED

• Quarterly Results: Total revenue increased 34.1% YoY and 14.5% QoQ to ₹294 Cr, EBITDA surged 70.3% YoY and 29.9% QoQ to ₹84 Cr, while PAT jumped 80.1% YoY and 35.5% QoQ to ₹63 Cr

• Margin Expansion: EBITDA margin improved to 28.6% from 22.5% YoY and 25.2% QoQ, supported by strong growth across high-voltage equipment businesses

• Order Book: Consolidated order book stood at approximately ₹2,010 Cr, providing revenue visibility across FY27 and beyond

• Order Book Breakdown: Endoks ₹800 Cr, Mehru ₹610 Cr, Quality Power ₹602 Cr and Others ₹5 Cr as of September 2026

• New Sangli Factory: Global Coil Factory commenced manufacturing on October 20, 2026, producing high-voltage reactors and specialised coils for HVAC, HVDC, FACTS and renewable energy applications

• Türkiye Manufacturing Expansion: Power Conversion Systems facility commenced operations on October 16, 2026, manufacturing converters and inverters for utility-scale Battery Energy Storage Systems

• Capacity Ramp-Up: Management plans to progressively scale production at both new facilities, improve manufacturing throughput and complete customer qualifications

• Winwin Acquisition: Signed agreement to acquire up to 100% of Winwin Speciality Insulators, subject to approvals, expanding its high-voltage transmission equipment portfolio

• Winwin Business Opportunities: Completed porcelain insulator testing up to 400 kV and secured qualifications and orders for 800 kV HVDC, 765 kV and 400 kV applications

• International Orders: Endoks secured a significant FACTS equipment order in Japan, while Mehru received multiple 400 kV instrument transformer orders from Hitachi Energy India

• US Data Centre Business: Received initial orders for high-voltage interconnection equipment for hyperscale and AI data centre campuses in the United States

• Global Order Pipeline: Growing opportunities in HVDC, FACTS, high-voltage equipment and grid-scale battery storage across the Americas, Europe, Middle East and Asia-Pacific

• H1 Performance: Total revenue increased 33.2% YoY to ₹550 Cr, EBITDA grew 52.2% to ₹149 Cr and PAT increased 52.4% to ₹110 Cr

• Future Growth Plans: Focused on grid modernisation, renewable integration, HVDC transmission, energy storage, international expansion and high-voltage manufacturing capabilities

• Operational Challenges: Copper, electrical-grade steel and specialised insulation costs remain key risks for manufacturing profitability and project execution

• FY27 Guidance & Capex: Management expects encouraging demand and continued capacity ramp-up but has not disclosed quantified FY27 revenue growth, EBITDA margin or fresh capex targets in this release

STUDDS ACCESSORIES Q2 FY27: TARGETS ₹1,000 CR REVENUE & 25–30% EXPORT SHARE; NEW 15 LAKH CAPACITY COMMISSIONED, PROFIT DOWN 29% YOY

• Medium-Term Revenue Target: Management aims to achieve ₹1,000 Cr revenue, with exports contributing 25–30% of total revenue

• Quarterly Results: Revenue increased 18.6% YoY and 7.90% QoQ to ₹183.1 Cr, while EBITDA declined 23.7% YoY but increased 16.92% QoQ to ₹22.8 Cr

• Profitability: PAT declined 28.5% YoY but increased 19.51% QoQ to ₹14.7 Cr

• Margin Pressure: EBITDA margin declined to 12.4% from 19.3% YoY, but improved from approximately 11.5% QoQ due to better sequential operating performance

• Capacity Expansion: New manufacturing facility commenced commercial production on October 30, 2026, adding 15 lakh units of annual helmet and box capacity

• Total Manufacturing Capacity: Installed capacity increased to 1.15 crore helmets and boxes annually across four manufacturing units

• European Expansion: Developing its wholly owned Italian subsidiary into a warehousing and distribution hub to strengthen its presence across Europe

• International Growth Plans: Targeting deeper market penetration across the US, Europe and Latin America through wider distribution and product diversification

• New Product Expansion: Commenced in-house manufacturing of riding jackets, expanding beyond its core helmet business

• Upcoming Product Launch: Bluetooth-enabled rider communication systems scheduled for launch in November 2026

• Export Realisations: Export average selling price increased to approximately ₹2,000 in H1 FY27 from ₹1,600 in FY24

• Premium Product Growth: SMK brand ASP improved to approximately ₹2,900 from ₹2,350 in FY24, reflecting stronger premium product realisations

• Raw Material Challenges: Higher crude oil and styrene-based input costs affected profitability, despite strong domestic and international demand

• Margin Recovery Plans: Implementing calibrated price increases, cost optimisation and operating efficiencies; sustained margin recovery depends on raw material price stabilisation

• H1 Performance: Revenue increased 16.2% YoY to ₹352.8 Cr, while EBITDA declined 29.6% to ₹42.3 Cr and PAT fell 33.8% to ₹27 Cr

• Future Growth Plans: Focused on increasing exports, ramping up new capacity, premiumisation, developing riding accessories and expanding international distribution

• FY27 Guidance & Capex: Management reiterated its medium-term ₹1,000 Cr revenue ambition but did not disclose specific FY27 growth, margin or fresh capex target

CAPILLARY : KPMG FORENSIC REPORT FLAGS EUR 3.04 MN FRAUD AT CZECH STEP-DOWN SUBSIDIARY

• Four disputed payments totalling EUR 3,041,169.90 made from Session M Czech Republic s.r.o. between 26 June and 2 July 2026
• Three payments routed to ZZDJB CO LIMITED at HSBC Hong Kong; one to ZHONGXIAN TRADING PTE. LTD at UOB Singapore
• Fraud executed via executive and legal-professional impersonation, lookalike domain law-ogier.co.uk, WhatsApp and personal email
• No malware, endpoint compromise, mailbox takeover or traditional spoofing found on the two reviewed laptops and records
• Deepfake use could neither be substantiated nor refuted as original audio, video and telecom metadata were unavailable
• Report received on 30 October 2026 and forwarded to Audit Committee and Board for review at ensuing meetings
Impact: Negative (EUR 3.04 MN first-hop diversion at step-down subsidiary; no technical compromise found, but payment-governance and beneficiary-validation gaps flagged)

Q2FY27 FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
- Revenue ₹390.1 Cr, up 23.1% YoY

H1FY27 FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
- Revenue ₹856.4 Cr, up 35.5% YoY

- EBITDA Margin 16%, down 42 bps YoY
- PAT ₹79 Cr, up 40.4% YoY
- PAT Margin 9.2%, up 32 bps YoY

ORDER BOOK AND BUSINESS UPDATE
- Order book stood at ₹3,196.97 Cr
- Enquiry pipeline reached ₹19,464 Cr
- Secured ₹193.92 Cr APTRANSCO Letter of Intent
- Order covers twelve 160 MVA, 220/132 kV auto transformers
- First order secured from the United States
- Demand supported by T&D and renewable energy
- Industrial applications also contributed to revenue growth

CAPACITY EXPANSION
- First 315 MVA, 400 kV transformer manufacturing commenced
- Short-circuit testing targeted by Q3FY27-end
- Dedicated Inverter Duty Transformer facility adds 5,000 MVA capacity
- Facility commissioning targeted by Q3FY27
- Tank and radiator backward integration progressing
- Investments underway in 400 kV and 765 kV transformers

EXECUTION AND MARGIN PRESSURES
- Heavy rainfall disrupted manufacturing and customer deliveries
- Approximately ₹180 Cr deliveries were deferred during Q2
- Around 70% of deferred deliveries completed subsequently
- Remaining deliveries expected during Q3FY27
- Elevated commodity prices pressured operating margins
- Firm-price contracts faced higher input-cost pressure
- Temporary production and dispatch disruptions affected profitability

MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY
- Management describes operational challenges as largely temporary
- Operations have normalised and dispatches are resuming
- Execution momentum expected to improve during H2FY27
- Strong order book provides revenue visibility
- US order marks an export milestone
- Renewable integration supports transformer demand
- Battery storage and grid infrastructure offer opportunities
- Management remains confident about India's T&D growth

KEY TAKEAWAYS
- Strong revenue and PAT growth during Q2
- EBITDA growth remained below revenue growth
- Commodity inflation pressured EBITDA margins
- Weather disruptions deferred significant customer deliveries
- Order book provides healthy business visibility
- First US order strengthens export opportunities
- Higher-voltage transformer capabilities are expanding
- Track deferred deliveries and margin recovery
- Monitor commissioning and execution of new capacities

SKY GOLD & DIAMONDS - Q2FY27 CONCALL HIGHLIGHTS
#Q2FY27

Q2FY27 FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
- Revenue ₹2,391 Cr, up 61% YoY and 18.8% QoQ
- Gross Profit ₹229 Cr, up 87% YoY
- Gross Margin 9.6%, expanding 133 bps YoY
- EBITDA ₹189 Cr, up 90% YoY
- EBITDA Margin stood at 7.9%
- Reported PAT ₹129 Cr, up 93% YoY
- Operational PAT ₹135 Cr, up 101% YoY
- Excludes exceptional charge

H1FY27 FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
- Revenue ₹4,403 Cr, up 68% YoY
- EBITDA ₹346 Cr
- PAT ₹234 Cr, up 112% YoY
- Operating Cash Flow ₹136 Cr
- Previous year's operating cash flow: ₹101 Cr outflow

BUSINESS AND PRODUCT MIX
- Advanced Gold contributed 16% of Q2 business
- Exceeded FY27 target of 15%
- Advanced Gold contributed approximately 120 bps gross margin
- Natural and lab-grown diamond jewellery contributed 2.5-2.6% revenue
- Focus on higher-margin studded and diamond jewellery
- Lightweight jewellery is 20-30% lighter
- Technology-led manufacturing supports lightweight products

EXPORTS AND INTERNATIONAL EXPANSION
- Q2 exports reached ₹435 Cr
- FY23 full-year exports were ₹35 Cr
- Exports now contribute approximately 18% of business
- Annualised export run rate approximately ₹1,600 Cr
- Dubai office supports expansion across GCC markets
- Expanding presence across Singapore and Malaysia
- Targeting Saudi Arabia, UK and Japan

WORKING CAPITAL AND DEBT
- Net working capital reduced to 55 days
- Previous working capital cycle: 63 days
- Net debt stood at ₹531 Cr
- March 2026 net debt: ₹550 Cr
- H1 operating cash flow conversion reached 58% of PAT
- Net interest cost declined to 0.89% of sales
- Previous net interest cost: 0.96%
- Receivable days stood at 33
- Festive receivables expected during October-November

ACQUISITIONS AND GROWTH STRATEGY
- Acquisitions target additional product categories
- Focus on management expertise and customer relationships
- Rishabh Gold Mangalsutra volumes reached 150 kg monthly
- Previous monthly volumes were 20-25 kg
- Rishabh Gold revenue increased to ₹175 Cr
- Previous revenue stood at ₹49 Cr
- Rishabh Gold profit increased to ₹18.8 Cr
- Previous profit stood at ₹1.6 Cr
- Management sees further industry consolidation opportunities

FUNDRAISING AND LAND MONETISATION
- Management discussed proposed ₹1,800 Cr fundraise
- Utilisation details remain undisclosed due to regulatory restrictions
- Land monetisation reached advanced due-diligence stage
- Prospective buyer discussions remain underway
- Promoters may acquire land without commitment
- Decision expected within 20-30 days

MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY
- No fresh forward guidance due to SEBI restrictions
- Historical PAT margin guidance remains 5-5.25%
- Management reiterated guidance remains on track
- Focus on exports and advanced gold products
- Priorities include margins and capital efficiency
- Operating cash flow remains a key priority
- Promoters linked salaries to operating cash flow generation

KEY TAKEAWAYS
- Strong revenue and profitability growth continued
- Advanced Gold exceeded its FY27 contribution target
- Export business reached 18% revenue contribution
- Operating cash flow turned positive during H1
- Working capital cycle improved to 55 days
- Debt declined compared with March 2026
- Rishabh Gold acquisition delivered significant growth
- Proposed ₹1,800 Cr fundraise requires monitoring
- Land monetisation remains subject to final commitment
- Track cash conversion, margins and debt levels

CAPILLARY : KPMG REPORT CONFIRMS EUR 3.04 MN PAYMENT FRAUD AT STEP-DOWN SUBSIDIARY

• Forensic report received October 30, 2026; four disputed payments totalling EUR 3,041,169.90 executed from Session M Czech Republic s.r.o. between June 26 and July 2, 2026
• Fraud carried out by external parties impersonating a senior executive and an outside lawyer via lookalike domain law-ogier.co.uk and off-channel WhatsApp and personal email
• Report finds no malware, endpoint compromise, mailbox takeover, traditional email spoofing, or questioned employee involvement
• Three payments routed to ZZDJB CO LIMITED at HSBC Hong Kong and one to ZHONGXIAN TRADING PTE LTD at UOB Singapore
• Deepfake voice or video use could neither be substantiated nor refuted; onward fund movement outside forensic scope
• Company says payment controls further strengthened and recovery and legal remedies actively pursued
Impact: Negative (EUR 3.04 mn fraud loss at step-down subsidiary with no recovery confirmed; governance overhang partly offset by clean technical and employee findings)

📢 Business Update – Patel Retail Limited

📍 Patel Retail to Expand Ambernath Distribution Centre by 20,000 Sq. Ft.; Total Area to Increase to 84,000 Sq. Ft.

Patel Retail Limited (BSE: 544487 | NSE: PATELRMART) proposes to develop approximately 20,000 sq. ft. of additional covered space at its existing distribution centre at Ambernath, Maharashtra, increasing the total area from 64,000 sq. ft. to 84,000 sq. ft.

🏬 Capacity Expansion: The proposed addition will increase the distribution centre's area by approximately 31% . The existing 64,000 sq. ft. capacity is currently operating at 100% utilisation. The additional space is expected to enhance the utilisation of the Company's existing infrastructure and strengthen its storage, packing and distribution capabilities.

📦 Strengthening Supply Chain: The expanded facility will enhance warehousing, storage, packaging and distribution operations , enabling smoother and more efficient replenishment of existing retail stores and helping maintain consistent product availability for customers.

📈 Supporting Future Growth: The additional capacity will support upcoming store openings under the Company's cluster-based expansion strategy. It will also provide greater inventory-holding capacity across product categories, including its private labels Indian Chaska, Patel Fresh, Tidymax, Blixo and others, enabling more efficient movement of products to stores.

🚀 Business Outlook: The initiative will strengthen the Company's supply chain, facilitate efficient inventory management and support the planned expansion of its retail network. By building capacity ahead of store additions, Patel Retail aims to maintain product availability, improve service levels and enhance operational efficiency as its network grows.

The expansion reinforces the Company's focus on strengthening its distribution infrastructure and bringing organised retail closer to customers across suburban and emerging urban markets.

PRATAAP SNACKS Q2 FY27: TARGETS STRONG DOUBLE-DIGIT FY27 REVENUE GROWTH; NEW INDORE MANUFACTURING PLANT & REVENUE UP 26% YOY

• FY27 Revenue Guidance: Management expects strong double-digit revenue growth, supported by core product demand, distribution expansion, new launches and alternate sales channels

• Quarterly Results: Revenue increased 25.9% YoY and 10.3% QoQ to ₹540.95 Cr, crossing the ₹500 Cr quarterly milestone for the first time

• Profitability: Operating EBITDA declined 43.7% YoY and 32.3% QoQ to ₹12.90 Cr, while PAT recorded a loss of ₹2.50 Cr versus profit of ₹4.64 Cr YoY and ₹2.47 Cr QoQ

• Margin Pressure: Operating EBITDA margin declined to 2.38% from approximately 5.33% YoY and 3.88% QoQ, due to elevated input costs

• New Manufacturing Facility: Acquired RLOP, securing leasehold land rights for the proposed greenfield manufacturing plant near Indore

• Project Execution: Site development and preparatory work have commenced, with civil construction and procurement of long-lead plant and machinery planned next

• Capacity Expansion: New plant expected to improve manufacturing efficiency, optimise operating costs and support future growth and margin improvement

• Product Growth: Strong momentum across Namkeen and Potato Chips, supported by encouraging demand for recently launched products

• Distribution Expansion: Strengthening reach through more than 5,000 distributors and sub-distributors across 27 states and 4 union territories

• Quick Commerce Growth: Expanding presence across quick commerce and modern trade channels to diversify revenue and improve market penetration

• Technology Investments: Sales Force Automation initiatives improving sales productivity, distribution efficiency and market coverage

• Raw Material Challenges: Higher palm oil, packaging laminate, fuel and logistics costs continue to pressure profitability

• Margin Recovery Plans: Implementing grammage rationalisation, selective channel-margin adjustments, trade scheme optimisation and cost-control measures

• Future Growth Plans: Focused on product innovation, expanding distribution, scaling alternate channels, commissioning new manufacturing infrastructure and improving operating margins

• Pyrolysis Oil Realizations: Tyre pyrolysis oil prices broadly track crude oil and industrial furnace oil prices.

• Pyrolysis Oil Price Risk: Management expects realizations to moderate if global energy prices normalize.

• Pyrova Revenue Diversification: Management is developing an integrated revenue model comprising tyre pyrolysis oil, crumb rubber, recovered steel, recovered carbon black and EPR credits.

• Integrated Recycling Model: Management expects the ability to recover value from multiple components of end-of-life tyres to support more stable profitability than a single-product recycling business.

• EPR Income Outlook: Management expects the EPR framework to remain an important revenue component as recycling capacities expand.

• EPR Regulatory Outlook: Management expects improved regulatory monitoring, audits and enforcement to support the formal tyre recycling ecosystem.

• EPR Sustainability: Management believes the tyre recycling EPR mechanism is relatively established compared with certain other recycling categories.

• EPR Compliance Challenges: Management highlighted the potential impact of credits generated by informal recyclers and the need for stronger regulatory oversight.

• Pyrolysis Raw Material Sourcing: Company uses domestically sourced end-of-life tyres for its pyrolysis operations.

• Pyrolysis Import Restrictions: Management clarified that imported waste tyres are not used in the pyrolysis business because of regulatory restrictions.

• Domestic Tyre Procurement: Company operates an integrated processing system with shredders, raspers and grinding equipment for end-of-life tyre recycling.

• Reclaimed Rubber Feedstock: The separate reclaimed rubber business uses a combination of domestic feedstock, market-purchased crumb rubber and permitted imported tyre waste.

• Imported Waste Regulations: Management indicated that eligible imports for reclaimed rubber operations are undertaken under applicable advance licences.

• Raw Material Procurement Outlook: Management expects securing adequate domestic end-of-life tyre feedstock to remain a key operational priority as pyrolysis capacity expands.

• New Technology Cost Savings: Management indicated that the new reclaimed rubber technology offers approximately 2–3% overall cost savings.

• Reclaimed Rubber Margin Outlook: Management expects increasing adoption of new processing technologies to support contribution margins despite raw material inflation.

KWALITY WALL'S: APPOINTS TAHIR TOLOY TANRIDAGLI AS MD & CEO FOR 3 YEARS

• Leadership Appointment: Appointed Tahir Toloy Tanridagli as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer

• Appointment Tenure: Three years from November 1, 2026, to October 31, 2029, subject to shareholder and applicable statutory approvals

• Industry Experience: Brings over 20 years of experience across FMCG, ice cream and consumer businesses

• Current Position: Serves on the Board of Kwality Wall's and holds a regional leadership role at The Magnum Ice Cream Company

• Business Transformation: Played a key role in Kwality Wall's transition following the demerger of Hindustan Unilever's ice cream business

• Global Experience: Previously held senior leadership positions at Unilever and Kraft Foods-Mondelez across multiple international markets

• Growth Strategy: Will focus on strengthening operational performance and developing Kwality Wall's ice cream business in India

• Leadership Expertise: Extensive experience in marketing, brand development, business operations and international expansion

Impact: Neutral to Positive (Experienced FMCG leadership and strong ice cream industry expertise could support operational efficiency, brand development and long-term business growth.)

**JEFFERIES ON INDIGO**

Target: ₹5,650
Earlier Target: ₹5,840
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Guides for low-single-digit ASK growth in FY27 and mid-teens capacity expansion in FY28
- Expects 25%+ PRASK growth in Q3, supported by disciplined capacity deployment
- Cuts FY27 EPS estimates by 9%; elevated fuel costs remain key earnings risk

**JEFFERIES ON INDIA STRATEGY**

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 mid-quarter review indicates upgrades holding up
- Results remain healthy, with upgrade ratio sustaining above 50%
- Banks, 2Ws, Power Utilities and consumer tech delivered well
- IT and staples remain mixed; 4Ws weak
- Management commentary indicates pockets of festive demand strength
- MSCI India FY27 earnings growth expectations upgraded 1 percentage point to 15%

**INVESTEC ON ACC & AMBUJA CEMENTS**

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Maintains Buy on Ambuja Cement, TP Rs 615; Hold on ACC, TP Rs 1,683
- Ambuja announces 29.7 MT grinding and 10.3 MT clinker capacity expansion at Rs 154 bn capex
- Targets cement capacity of 149 MT by FY29 and 155 MT by FY30; expects H2 volume growth ahead of industry
- Captive fly ash and fiscal incentives offer cost advantages; execution and cost guidance remain key concerns

**MORGAN STANLEY ON COAL INDIA**

Target: ₹480
Recommendation: Overweight

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Strong thermal power demand and five-year-low coal inventories support an earnings upgrade cycle
- Elevated global coal prices could drive higher e-auction premiums and realisations
- Expects sustained demand recovery, supported by low power-plant coal stocks and rising international prices

**UBS ON INDIGO**

Target: ₹5,050
Earlier Target: ₹5,450
Recommendation: Neutral

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Guides for low-single-digit ASK growth in FY27 and 25%+ PRASK growth in Q3
- Targets ~300 bn ASKs by FY30, supported by international expansion and long-haul operations
- Cuts FY27/FY28 EBITDA estimates by 7%/20%; raises FY29 estimates by 6% on fuel-cost normalisation

**NOMURA ON INDIGO**

Target: ₹6,200
Earlier Target: ₹6,000
Recommendation: Neutral

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Expects 30% PRASK growth in Q3, with pricing recovering 80–90% of fuel-cost inflation
- Forecasts FY28 EBITDA margin expansion to 21%, supported by lower fuel prices and fleet growth
- Raises FY27/FY28 EBITDA estimates by 11%/3%; expects 40% EBITDA CAGR over FY26–29

**HSBC ON INDIGO**

Target: ₹5,545
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Guides for 25%+ PRASK growth and low-single-digit capacity expansion in FY27
- Expects ex-fuel unit costs to rise high-single to low-double digits; international capacity growth to moderate
- Ancillary, cargo, business class and BluChip loyalty programme remain growth priorities; targets mid-teens capacity growth in FY28

**HSBC ON ASIAN PAINTS**

Target: ₹2,420
Earlier Target: ₹2,650
Recommendation: Hold

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Retains FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18–20%; rising input costs and competition threaten recovery
- Premiumisation and festive demand offer support, but dealer promotions and consumer downgrading remain risks
- Cuts target valuation multiple to 40x from 45x; questions potential savings from backward integration

**GOLDMAN SACHS ON CRAFTSMAN AUTOMATION**

Target: ₹13,000
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue/EBITDA/net profit grow 47%/30%/68% YoY; results broadly in line
- EBITDA margin contracts 178 bps YoY to 13.3% amid input-cost pressures
- New production launches, higher-CC engine mix and Sunbeam margin recovery to support H2 growth
- Cuts FY27–29 EPS estimates by 2% each; expects stronger growth from Tata Motors-Stellantis partnership

**KOTAK ON LAURUS LABS**

Target: ₹1,400
Recommendation: Sell

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Expects ~34% EBITDA CAGR over FY26–29, with margins reaching ~36% by FY29
- Plans Rs 30 bn-plus capex over FY27–28, largely targeting high-growth projects
- Peptides, oligonucleotides and advanced therapies expand CDMO opportunities; valuations remain a concern

**GOLDMAN SACHS ON PIDILITE INDUSTRIES**

Target: ₹1,700
Earlier Target: ₹1,850
Recommendation: Buy

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Q2 revenue rises 20.9% YoY; EBITDA grows 3.1%, missing estimates by 6.4%
- Underlying volume growth at 10.7%; gross margin contracts 650 bps YoY on higher input costs
- Additional 3–5% price hikes and easing VAM prices expected to support H2 margin recovery
- Cuts FY27–29 EPS estimates by 1–1.7%; expects FY27 EBITDA margin at higher end of 20–24% guidance

**KOTAK ON RR KABEL**

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Cuts FY27 W&C volume growth guidance to 14–15% from 18% earlier
- Retains FY27 W&C EBIT margin guidance at 9.5%; targets FMEG operating breakeven
- Raises FY27–29 earnings estimates by 7–9%; flags intensifying competition

**KOTAK ON HEXAWARE TECHNOLOGIES**

**JIO PLATFORMS – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**NOMURA: INITIATE BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹1,340**
- Jio has evolved from a market disruptor into a market leader.
- Holds 42% of India's wireless subscribers, 60% of data traffic and 43% of home broadband.
- Expects the listing to support Jio's position as a tariff price-setter, enabling steady tariff hikes that competitors can follow.
- Estimates 13.5% EBITDA CAGR over FY26–FY29.
- Strong network and subscriber leadership support long-term value creation.
- Home broadband is expected to become the second major growth engine.
- Global technology licensing offers additional long-term growth potential.
- With most 5G capex largely completed, lower capex intensity could drive a sharp improvement in free cash flow.

**MOTILAL OSWAL (MOSL): INITIATE BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹1,350**
- Jio Platforms is India's largest digital connectivity platform, with Reliance Jio serving 533 million subscribers.
- Expects wireless revenue market share to increase by 100 bps to 43.3% by FY29.
- Forecasts Jio to account for 73% of incremental home broadband industry net additions over FY26–FY29.
- Digital growth opportunities include cloud, enterprise communications, IoT, managed services and international partnerships for 5G/UBR technology.
- Forecasts FY26–FY29 CAGR of:
  - Revenue: 14%
  - Reported EBITDA: 15%
  - PAT: 20%
- Growth drivers include subscriber additions, approximately 15% tariff hikes from March 2027, home broadband expansion and scaling digital platform offerings.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Both brokerages initiate coverage with Buy ratings, highlighting Jio's leadership, pricing power and digital ecosystem.
- Tariff hikes, home broadband growth and digital services are expected to drive earnings expansion.
- Lower 5G capex intensity could improve free cash flow and support future value creation.
- Target prices: ₹1,340 (Nomura) and ₹1,350 (MOSL).

**LARSEN & TOUBRO (L&T) – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**CLSA: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹4,842**
- Q2 FY27 beat three of four guidance parameters: order inflows, execution and working capital; margins missed expectations.
- E&C execution increased 22% YoY despite Middle East disruptions, driven by 26% growth in the Middle East and 16% growth in India.
- Middle East order inflows rebounded strongly.
- Backlog reached US$90 billion, up 28% YoY, providing strong revenue visibility.
- FY27 guidance retained: 10–12% growth in new orders and execution, with flat margins.
- L&T has begun executing its FY31 strategy, expanding into AI, electronics manufacturing, green technology and chemicals.
- Won India's largest Nvidia AI factory order, supporting its AI infrastructure ambitions.

**MACQUARIE: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹4,710**
- Revenue grew 16% YoY and PAT increased 33% YoY.
- EBITDA remained broadly flat as margins declined 130 bps YoY to 8.7%, reflecting cost escalations.
- Record quarterly order intake and backlog growth of 28% each, led by international orders.
- Core order inflows grew 32% YoY.
- Management retained FY27 guidance despite Gulf-region challenges and improving private-sector participation in India's capex cycle.

**NOMURA: NEUTRAL | TARGET PRICE: ₹3,940**
- Execution and order inflows beat expectations, but margins disappointed.
- International execution was stronger than expected, while cost pressures persisted.
- H1 FY27 order inflows grew 22% YoY.
- FY27 order inflow growth guidance remains unchanged at 10–12%.
- Consolidated EBITDA was 7% below Nomura's estimate and 2% below consensus, despite 1% YoY growth.
- Valuation stands at 20.2x FY28 estimated EPS and 17.5x FY29 estimated EPS.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Strong execution, record order inflows and a US$90 billion backlog reinforce L&T's growth visibility.
- Margin compression from cost escalation remains the key near-term concern.
- AI, electronics manufacturing and green technology offer potential long-term growth opportunities.
- Brokerage views are largely positive: CLSA and Macquarie maintain Outperform ratings, while Nomura remains Neutral.
- Target prices: ₹4,842 (CLSA), ₹4,710 (Macquarie) and ₹3,940 (Nomura).

**MARUTI SUZUKI – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**HSBC: BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹14,500**
- Demand commentary remains strong, with management guiding for 10% domestic wholesale growth in H2 FY27.
- Margin recovery may be gradual as price hikes remain cautious.
- Margin improvement depends partly on a moderation in commodity costs.
- Valuations appear reasonable, with declining commodity prices identified as a key trigger.

**NOMURA: BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹13,046**
- Q2 FY27 performance was broadly in line with expectations.
- EBITDA margin stood at 8.9%, versus Nomura's estimate of 8.8%.
- Strong H2 FY27 guidance supports near-term demand visibility.
- Potential slowdown in FY28 remains a risk.
- Electric vehicle (EV) contribution is an important metric for the stock's performance.

**CLSA: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹14,537**
- Q2 EBITDA margin reached 8.9%, up 71 bps QoQ, ahead of consensus.
- Margin improvement was driven by cost-reduction measures, price hikes and the retail-wholesale gap.
- Management expects 10% domestic portfolio growth in H2 FY27, with exports broadly flat, implying overall volume growth of approximately 7–10%.
- CLSA remains conservative, factoring in 5% volume growth for H2 FY27.
- Inventory stood below normal at 17 days, while the order book reached 2.7 lakh units after Dussehra.
- Management remains confident of achieving its 10% domestic volume growth guidance.
- Commodity costs are expected to remain broadly flat QoQ in Q3 FY27, supporting a gradual EBITDA margin recovery.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Strong domestic demand, low inventory and a healthy order book support H2 FY27 volume growth.
- Margin recovery depends on cost control, pricing and commodity trends.
- FY28 demand sustainability and EV contribution remain important monitorables.
- All three brokerages are positive, with target prices ranging from ₹13,046 to ₹14,537.

Motilal Oswal: Rating Buy Tgt: 1350/Sh**

**BAJAJ AUTO – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**CLSA: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹13,446**
- Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin stood at 20.9%, flat QoQ despite 3–3.5% commodity inflation.
- Cost pressures were offset by currency depreciation, richer product mix, higher PLI benefits, calibrated price hikes, operating leverage and cost-reduction measures.
- Potential margin headwinds include a higher electric two-wheeler mix, adverse currency movement in Q3 and further commodity inflation of approximately 2%.
- Refreshed Pulsar models across segments and two new brand launches in the 125–150cc motorcycle segment could support growth.
- Strong demand in motorcycles above 150cc and higher electric scooter capacity may help improve market share.

**JPMORGAN: UPGRADED TO OVERWEIGHT | TARGET PRICE: ₹12,500**
- Positive outlook driven by better-than-expected EV volume ramp-up and profitability.
- Export growth remains strong, supported by diversified markets across Africa, Latin America and ASEAN, with further expansion planned.
- Two new platforms expected in CY27 will cover the 125–250cc motorcycle segment, broader than JPMorgan's earlier expectation of only 125cc.
- Bajaj Auto is among the few automobile OEMs to receive earnings upgrades over the past 12 months despite commodity headwinds.
- FY27–FY29 EPS estimates raised by 5–8%.
- Stock trades at 19x FY28 estimated P/E versus its five-year average of 22x.
- Expected FY26–FY29 EPS CAGR: 17%.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Strong exports, improving EV economics and upcoming product launches are key growth drivers.
- Commodity inflation, currency movements and a higher EV mix remain potential margin risks.
- Both brokerages remain positive, with target prices of ₹13,446 (CLSA) and ₹12,500 (JPMorgan).

**SBI LIFE INSURANCE – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**HSBC: BUY | TARGET PRICE: ₹2,088**
- Q2 FY27 APE growth was muted, but sharp margin expansion partly offset the pressure on VNB.
- VNB came in 2% below HSBC estimates.
- Management retained its APE growth and margin guidance.
- HSBC expects mid-teens APE and VNB CAGR over the medium term.
- Views SBI Life as a strong long-term compounding opportunity.

**MACQUARIE: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹2,120**
- VNB grew 12% YoY, broadly in line with expectations.
- VNB margin reached 29.2%, or 30% excluding the GST impact, versus Macquarie's 26% estimate.
- Total APE grew 8% YoY, below Macquarie's 14% estimate.
- Retail APE growth moderated to 10% YoY.
- ULIP growth slowed to 4% amid weak markets.
- Non-par guaranteed products grew 27%, reflecting stronger demand.
- Retail protection grew 14% on a strong base, while participating (par) business declined 4%.
- Management expects retail growth to accelerate in H2 FY27.
- FY27 retail growth guidance retained at 14–15%, versus 11% in H1.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Strong VNB margin expansion supported value creation despite slower APE growth.
- Recovery in retail business growth during H2 FY27 is a key monitorable.
- Both brokerages remain positive, with target prices of ₹2,088 (HSBC) and ₹2,120 (Macquarie).

Is India to be World's Oil Refiner?

India is the world's fourth-largest refiner and is heading toward 6.66 million barrels a day by 2032, providing crucial leverage in the global energy market.

However, shifting crude economics, potential sanctions, and the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism pose structural risks to India's long-term refining ambitions.

**CIPLA – BROKERAGE VIEWS**

**HSBC: HOLD | TARGET PRICE: ₹1,400**
- Q2 FY27 performance was lacklustre.
- Retains FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18.5–20%.
- Maintains target of achieving a US$1 billion annualised US sales exit run-rate in FY27.
- Opportunity from key US launches, including inhalers, remains intact.
- High execution requirements create risks to achieving FY27 guidance.
- Execution of key US launches remains critical.

**CLSA: OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹1,600**
- Q2 FY27 revenue marginally missed estimates despite Cipla India delivering its best-ever performance, driven by GLP-1 product Yurpeak.
- Margins improved QoQ due to a better product mix.
- Reiterated US$1 billion annualised US sales exit run-rate target for FY27.
- Growth expected from three new launches and the ramp-up of generic Ventolin and Advair.
- Plans to file 45–50 complex products in the US over the next three years.
- Expects steady India growth, supported by continued traction in Yurpeak.
- Retained FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18.5–20%, with US performance expected to improve.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- India business momentum and QoQ margin improvement are positives.
- Achieving the US sales target depends heavily on successful launches and execution.
- Brokerage views differ: HSBC remains on Hold, while CLSA maintains an Outperform rating.
- Target prices: ₹1,400 (HSBC) vs ₹1,600 (CLSA).

**INDUS TOWERS – BROKERAGE VIEWS**
**HSBC: REDUCE | TARGET PRICE: ₹345**
- Revenue and EBITDA came in line with estimates.
- Net profit missed estimates due to higher depreciation.
- Colocation net additions for H1 FY27 stood at approximately 12,000.

**CLSA: HIGH-CONVICTION OUTPERFORM | TARGET PRICE: ₹565**
- Q2 FY27 core revenue: ₹5,450 Cr, up 4% YoY and 1% QoQ, in line with estimates.
- Core adjusted EBITDA grew 5% YoY and 2% QoQ, ahead of estimates.
- Net tenancy additions jumped to 7,903 vs 4,236 in Q1 FY27, beating estimates despite delays in Vodafone Idea's fundraising.
- Added 2,869 towers during Q2, taking the total tower count to 2,70,480.
- Core EBITDA CAGR of 9% projected through FY29 by CLSA.
- H1 FY27 capex declined 9% YoY to ₹4,100 Cr.
- Free cash flow increased 51% QoQ to ₹2,810 Cr.
- Balance sheet remained net cash positive at ₹3,400 Cr.

**KEY TAKEAWAY**
- Operational performance and tenancy additions were strong, with CLSA highlighting growth visibility and cash generation.
- HSBC remains cautious, citing the net profit miss due to higher depreciation.
- Brokerage views are sharply divided: HSBC has a ₹345 target, while CLSA has a ₹565 target.

**LT FOODS LTD - H1FY27 RESULTS**
#H1FY27

**FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE**
- Consolidated Revenue ₹6,414 Cr, up 22% YoY
- EBITDA ₹721 Cr, up 17% YoY
- PAT ₹364 Cr, up 9% YoY

**BUSINESS-WISE PERFORMANCE**
- India business grew 24% YoY, driven by premiumisation and portfolio expansion
- Basmati and Other Specialty Rice business grew 27% YoY
- North America business grew 20.8%
- Royal brand maintained over 60% market share in North America

**GLOBAL EXPANSION**
- Acquired 70.75% controlling stake in Netherlands-based Leev.nu B.V.
- Acquisition completed through organic foods arm Nature Bio Foods
- Investment consideration stood at €1.735 million

**PRODUCT LAUNCHES AND MARKET POSITION**
- DAAWAT Delight and Biryani Masala Paste received encouraging customer response
- DAAWAT Quick Cooking Brown Rice holds over 70% market share in its category
- Golden Star launched Microwaveable Rice Cups in the US
- Entry into the Ready-to-Heat (RTH) segment

**ESG PERFORMANCE**
- CRISIL ESG rating improved to 61 from 54
- Rating category upgraded to Strong

**MANAGEMENT OUTLOOK**
- Focus on building a stronger, future-ready global FMCG business
- Emphasis on sustainable and profitable growth

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Strong H1 revenue growth, with EBITDA growing faster than PAT
- India and specialty rice businesses delivered healthy growth
- North America continued to expand, supported by Royal's strong market position
- Acquisition of Leev.nu strengthens the company's international organic foods presence
- New product launches support portfolio diversification
- Monitor margin performance, PAT growth and integration of the overseas acquisition

**VARDHMAN SPECIAL STEELS LTD - Q2FY27 RESULTS**
#Q2FY27

**FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE**
- Revenue from Operations ₹600.05 Cr, up 38.81% YoY
- Total Income ₹614.79 Cr, up 38.62% YoY
- EBITDA ₹83.86 Cr, up 48.48% YoY
- PAT ₹52.49 Cr, up 51.88% YoY
- Basic EPS ₹5.43, up 50.42% YoY
- Rolled product sales volume reached 70,440 tonnes vs 55,536 tonnes YoY
- EBITDA per tonne stood at ₹11,346 on rolled sales quantity, excluding non-operational income

**KEY DRIVERS**
- Strong customer demand and improved realisations
- Higher sales volumes and better operating leverage
- Cost optimisation and operational efficiencies
- Benefit from lower-cost raw material inventory
- Progressive benefits from Kocks Block and reheating furnace capex
- Higher GST refund

**FORGING FACILITY AND STRATEGIC EXPANSION**
- Foundation stone laid for a new forging facility in Ludhiana with Aichi Steel Corporation
- Forward integration into higher-value forged components
- Focus on strengthening core operations and expanding value-added products
- Greenfield special steel facility planned
- Diversification into railways, oil & gas and other industrial segments
- Aichi Steel's stake increased to 24.90%, strengthening technology collaboration and Toyota-linked demand opportunities

**BALANCE SHEET AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2026**
- Equity ₹1,338.40 Cr
- Current borrowings ₹162.93 Cr
- Non-current assets ₹768.31 Cr
- Current assets ₹1,020.37 Cr

**LONG-TERM TRANSFORMATION PLAN**
- **Stage 1:** Automotive-focused steel business, with approximately 100% of revenue from automotive
- **Stage 2 (FY27-FY30):** Capacity and technology expansion, including ingot casting pilot and a 500,000-600,000 TPA greenfield plant
- **Stage 3 (FY35 target):** Approximately 1 million tonnes of steel capacity
- Target revenue mix of 70% automotive and 25-30% non-automotive by FY35
- Forging expansion capex budgeted at ₹475 Cr
- Target forging EBITDA margin of 15-20%
- Committed capex of approximately ₹2,600 Cr during FY26-FY30
- Target debt-to-equity ratio of 0.75x or lower

**COMPETITIVE STRENGTHS**
- Advanced manufacturing facilities and R&D capabilities
- Diversified products with applications across multiple sectors
- Experienced management in the special steel industry
- Stringent quality standards and established customer relationships
- 200+ customers, including Toyota, Hero MotoCorp and Maruti

**ESG INITIATIVES**
- 40 MW AC solar plant supporting decarbonisation
- Net-zero target by 2050
- Carbon intensity reduced to 0.45-0.48 tonnes of CO₂ per tonne
- CSR programmes covering women empowerment, education, healthcare, environmental conservation and sports
- Board includes 7 independent directors
- B S R & Co LLP serves as statutory auditor

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Strong Q2 growth across revenue, EBITDA and PAT
- Higher sales volumes and operating leverage supported profitability
- EBITDA per tonne reached ₹11,346
- Forging facility represents a move towards higher-value components
- Greenfield capacity and sector diversification are central to the long-term strategy
- Significant planned capex requires disciplined execution and balance-sheet management
- Monitor forging project execution, capacity utilisation, customer diversification and debt levels

**PAYTM - INVESTEC ANALYSIS**
#Q2FY27

**GROWTH AND PROFITABILITY**
- Net revenue excluding PIDF and UPI grew 35% YoY
- Financial Services (FS) revenue grew 49% YoY
- Overall EBITDA increased 33% QoQ to ₹270 Cr
- EBITDA came approximately 7% above Investec's estimates
- Estimated net payment processing margin improved to 5.1 bps from 4.7 bps QoQ
- GMV remained flat QoQ as the company prioritised higher-margin payment volumes

**FINANCIAL SERVICES OUTLOOK**
- Management expects the share of FLDG-linked loans to increase going forward
- Higher FLDG-linked loan mix could put pressure on reported contribution margins
- Strong Financial Services growth is expected to support absolute EBITDA expansion

**EARNINGS ESTIMATES**
- FY27E EBITDA cut by 5% due to delayed UPI MDR implementation
- FY28-29E EBITDA estimates remain unchanged despite higher promotional spending
- Stronger Financial Services revenue is expected to offset higher promotional costs
- PAT estimates cut by 16% for FY27E and 3-4% for FY28-29E
- PAT estimate reductions mainly reflect lower other income and marginally higher depreciation and amortisation

**VALUATION AND TARGET PRICE**
- Investec retains its target price of ₹2,300
- Valuation rolled forward to September 2028 estimates
- Implied valuation multiple reduced to 36x Sep-28E EV/EBITDA from 40x Jun-28E
- Cost of equity assumption increased

**KEY TAKEAWAYS**
- Strong revenue growth led by Financial Services
- EBITDA exceeded Investec's estimates
- Higher-margin payment mix improved estimated processing margins despite flat QoQ GMV
- Delayed UPI MDR implementation affects FY27 EBITDA expectations
- Higher FLDG-linked lending may pressure contribution margins, while supporting loan-related revenue growth
- Investec retains its ₹2,300 target price despite reducing PAT estimates

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
